orphans.title: Orphan Sponsorship
orphans.shortDescription: Monthly support that covers food, clothing, healthcare and schooling for orphaned children.
orphans.overviewDescription: Monthly support that covers food, clothing, healthcare and schooling for a named orphaned child. Sponsors receive progress reports and stay with the child until their education is complete.
orphans.subheading: Standing with a child until they can stand on their own.
orphans.aboutHeading: A commitment measured in years, not months
orphans.aboutOne: Losing a parent rarely costs a child only one thing. School fees go first, then medical care, then the small dignities that let a child sit in a classroom without shame. Our sponsorship program treats the whole of that loss rather than one part of it.
orphans.aboutTwo: Each sponsored child is registered with their guardian, assessed for what the household actually needs, and matched to a sponsor who commits to monthly support. Funds reach the guardian directly and are reconciled against receipts every term.
orphans.aboutThree: Sponsorship runs until the child finishes their education. We do not close a file because a funding cycle ended, and where a sponsor has to step away we carry the child ourselves until a new sponsor is found.
orphans.stepsHeading: From first visit to final report

registration.title: Registration
registration.description: A field volunteer visits the household, verifies the circumstances with the guardian and the local imam, and records the child.

matching.title: Sponsorship matching
matching.description: The child is matched to a sponsor, who receives a profile covering their age, schooling and the specific needs identified.

support.title: Monthly support
support.description: Funds are delivered to the guardian each month for food, clothing, healthcare and school costs, against signed receipts.

reports.title: Progress reports
reports.description: Sponsors receive termly updates on schooling and health, with photographs shared only where the guardian consents.

orphans.ctaDescription: Talk to us about sponsoring a named child, or about contributing to the shared fund that covers children still waiting for a sponsor.

mosques.title: Mosque Construction
mosques.shortDescription: Building and renovating places of worship that serve as the centre of community life.
mosques.overviewDescription: Building and renovating places of worship that serve as the centre of community life. Every mosque is built to last, with ablution facilities and, where the village needs one, a borehole.
mosques.subheading: A place to pray, and a place for a community to gather.
mosques.aboutOne: In many of the villages we work in, the mosque is the only public building. It is where disputes are settled, where children learn to read, and where news reaches everyone at once. Building one well changes far more than the Friday prayer.
mosques.aboutTwo: We build in blockwork with a roof designed for the rains, install ablution facilities, and sink a borehole where the community has no clean water. Local labour is hired and paid, so the construction itself puts money into the village.

survey.title: Community survey
survey.description: We meet the village elders, confirm the land is properly donated or titled, and agree the size the community can maintain.

build.title: Construction
build.description: Local builders are contracted and supervised to completion, with costs and photographs recorded at every stage.

handover.title: Handover
handover.description: The mosque is handed to the community with a maintenance plan, and revisited within the year to check how it is holding up.

mosques.ctaHeading: Fund a mosque in your name
mosques.ctaDescription: A full mosque, a roof, a borehole or a single course of blocks. Contact us and we will show you what each level of support builds.

schools.title: School Construction
schools.shortDescription: Classrooms, furniture and learning materials that put education within reach of every child.
schools.overviewDescription: Classrooms, furniture and learning materials that put education within reach of every child. We build where the nearest school is too far to walk, then stay involved after the doors open.
schools.subheading: Putting a classroom within walking distance of every child.
schools.aboutHeading: The building is only the beginning
schools.aboutOne: A school with no desks, no books and no teacher is a building, not an education. Our construction program budgets for what happens after the roof goes on, because that is where most school projects quietly fail.
schools.aboutTwo: We build classrooms in communities where the nearest school is an hour on foot, and we equip them with desks, boards and materials for the first full academic year. Where possible the school is sited beside an existing mosque so the two reinforce each other.
schools.aboutThree: We then stay in contact with the head teacher, track enrolment term by term, and return to repair what the weather has damaged. A school we built ten years ago is still our responsibility.

need.title: Needs assessment
need.description: We count the children in the catchment, measure the distance to the nearest school, and confirm the community will staff it.

construction.title: Construction
construction.description: Classrooms, latrines and a water point are built by contracted local labour under our supervision.

equip.title: Equipping
equip.description: Desks, boards, textbooks and teaching materials are supplied for the first full academic year.

followUp.title: Follow-up
followUp.description: Enrolment is tracked each term and the buildings are inspected annually, with repairs funded by the foundation.

schools.ctaHeading: Build a classroom that outlasts us
schools.ctaDescription: Fund a classroom, a set of desks or a full school. Contact us for the current list of communities waiting on a build.

hadiya.title: Ramadan & Eid Hadiya
hadiya.shortDescription: Seasonal food parcels and gifts delivered to families in hardship during Ramadan and Eid.
hadiya.overviewDescription: Seasonal food parcels and gifts delivered to families in hardship during Ramadan and Eid. Parcels are sized to the household and delivered to the door, never handed out from a queue.
hadiya.subheading: Making sure no household breaks its fast on nothing.
hadiya.aboutHeading: Delivered to the door, not to a queue
hadiya.aboutOne: Ramadan is the hardest month of the year for a household with no income. Prices rise, work is scarce, and the families least able to cope are the ones least likely to ask. Our distribution is built around finding them rather than waiting for them.
hadiya.aboutTwo: Parcels are sized to the household and carried to the door, so that no family has to stand in a line to be fed. On the day of Eid, children in the same households receive clothes and a small gift, because a festival a child cannot join is not much of a festival.

identify.title: Identifying households
identify.description: Ward heads and local imams help us list the households in genuine need, which we verify by visit before Ramadan begins.

pack.title: Packing
pack.description: Staples are bought in bulk at market rates and packed into parcels sized to each household, with costs published afterwards.

deliver.title: Delivery
deliver.description: Volunteers deliver to the door through the month, and return on Eid with clothes and gifts for the children.

hero.title: Trust. Transparency. Impact.
hero.description: For over a decade, Sharif Charity Foundation has served orphans, built mosques and schools, and delivered hope to families across Nigeria and beyond. Every donation traceable. Every project verified. Every trust honored.

mission.heading: Faith in action, backed by proof
mission.paragraphOne: We exist to turn the generosity of our donors into lasting relief for the people who need it most. Orphans are sponsored through to adulthood, mosques and schools are built to serve whole communities, and families in hardship are supported with dignity.
mission.paragraphTwo: Charity given in trust must be accounted for. Every project we undertake is documented from the first contribution to the final handover, so that donors can see exactly where their giving went and what it changed.

verifiability.description: Every project is documented with photographs, receipts and named beneficiaries that donors can check.

traceability.description: Each donation is recorded against the specific project it funded, from receipt through to delivery.

independence.description: We accept no political or partisan funding, so our decisions answer only to need on the ground.

accountability.description: Our accounts are reviewed and published, and every enquiry about spending receives a direct answer.

privacy.description: Beneficiaries are treated with dignity, and no family is photographed or named without consent.

continuity.description: Sponsorships and projects are seen through to completion rather than abandoned mid-way.

cta.heading: Ready to make an impact?
cta.description: Contact us today to sponsor an orphan, fund a project, or partner with us.

hero.heading: Our story, our purpose
hero.subheading: How the Sharif Charity Foundation came to be, and where we are going.

story.heading: From personal service to an institution
story.paragraphOne: Placeholder narrative. The foundation began with a small circle of families in Kano pooling what they could to keep orphaned children in school. There was no office and no letterhead, only a list of names and a promise that the help would not stop halfway.
story.paragraphTwo: Placeholder narrative. That work brought the founder alongside established international Islamic charities, first as a volunteer and later as the person trusted to carry their programmes into communities that outside organisations found hard to reach.
story.paragraphThree: Placeholder narrative. Years of field delivery followed, handing out food parcels in Ramadan, supervising borehole and mosque projects, and sitting with widows to work out what a household actually needed. The lesson from that decade was simple: generosity fails when nobody is accountable for the last mile.
story.paragraphFour: Placeholder narrative. Formalising the foundation was the answer to that lesson. The aim now is an institution rooted in Nigeria that can be audited, inherited and trusted, serving orphans, mosques, schools and families at a scale one person could never reach alone.

faith.description: Charity is an act of worship before it is an act of administration, and we treat every trust placed with us accordingly.

integrity.title: Integrity
integrity.description: What we promise a donor and what reaches a beneficiary are the same thing, documented at every step.

excellence.title: Excellence
excellence.description: A mosque, a classroom or a food parcel is built to last, because work done poorly wastes the giving behind it.

service.title: Service
service.description: We go to the households that are hardest to reach, and we treat the people we serve as neighbours rather than cases.

pillars.heading: Six pillars of donor trust
pillars.subheading: The commitments that govern how every naira entrusted to us is handled.

verifiability.description: Every project is documented with photographs, receipts and named beneficiaries. Donors may ask to see the file behind any project we have published. Where a claim cannot be evidenced, we do not make it.

traceability.description: Each donation is recorded against the specific project it funded, from the moment it is received to the day the work is handed over. Pooled giving is allocated openly rather than absorbed into a general fund. A donor can follow their contribution end to end.

independence.description: We accept no political or partisan funding, and no donation that carries conditions on who may benefit. Decisions about where to work answer to assessed need on the ground. That independence is what lets us go where others will not.

accountability.description: Our accounts are reviewed and published, and every enquiry about spending receives a direct answer with figures attached. Mistakes are reported rather than buried. Trustees carry personal responsibility for the integrity of the record.

privacy.description: Beneficiaries are treated with dignity, and no family is photographed, named or filmed without informed consent. Children are never used as fundraising imagery. Records that identify a household are held securely and shared with no one.

continuity.description: Sponsorships run until a child completes their education, not until the funding cycle ends. Construction projects are seen through to handover and then revisited. We commit only to what we are able to finish.

impact.heading: Funds and impact at a glance

segregation.title: Fund Segregation
segregation.description: Money given for a named project is held separately from general operating funds and cannot be spent on anything else. A donation for a school builds that school, even if another programme is short.

signatories.title: Multi-Signatory Approval
signatories.description: No single person can move foundation money. Every disbursement above a set threshold requires two trustee signatures and a written justification filed against the project.

audit.title: External Audit
audit.description: Our accounts are prepared for review by an independent auditor outside the foundation. The auditor reports to the trustees, and the findings are published rather than circulated internally.

reports.heading: Annual reports
reports.subheading: Each year of accounts, published in full once the audit is complete.
reports.caption: Annual reports and their publication status
reports.note: Reports will be posted here as each audit is completed.

governance.heading: Who decides, and who checks
governance.paragraphOne: Placeholder text. The foundation is directed by a board of trustees that sets policy, approves the annual budget and carries legal responsibility for how funds are used. Trustees serve fixed terms and are not paid for their service.
governance.paragraphTwo: Placeholder text. An audit committee drawn from outside the operational team reviews spending against the approved budget each quarter, and has standing authority to request any document or receipt without notice.
governance.paragraphThree: Placeholder text. Day-to-day delivery sits with an operational leadership team that reports to the board monthly. Field coordinators in each state report into that team and are responsible for the records behind every project.
